Just for grins, and because it’s been bugging me, I decided to come up with an idea for a “foolproof” vote tabulation system.

It works as follows:

A voter registers in one state-level system prior to the election using tax ID information. That state system corroborates with other states via Social Security, DOB and name correlation. The process is authenticated through the state income tax system (not an endorsement of the income tax, just using the pre-existing tools), because, let’s face it the records the states care most about are tax records, and if you haven’t filed your taxes as a resident of the state what business do you have voting there? The voter roll system generates an encrypted hex value registration ID.

Each election year, a voter is provided a second encrypted unique election year voter ID value (hex) that, when run through a decryption algorithm at polling places can be used to validate against the central system against a proper photo identification with matching address and name, basically a two hop system - decrypting the election year voter ID to retrieve the registration ID and then decrypting the registration ID to retrieve the address and other relevant validation info. This voter ID number must be presented and verified at time of ballot receipt along with state issued photo ID.

The ballot would feature no identifying marks other than the encrypted ID number, the state issuing and the date of the election in which the voter was participating.

So, John Smith of Kentucky, SSN 111-11-1111, DOB 1967-03-15 registers with his income tax return and is logged in the state system internally as KY-12345-ABCDEF-9876 and in 2020 receives the voter ID encrypted value of KY-AF11-11BD-23CE-4689-2020.

On Election Day of 2020, that being November 3, he carries his registration card with hex ID and barcode for scanning to the polling station, shows his photo ID to confirm his registration information, and is handed a ballot marked at the top with his hex code and the date of the general election:

KY-AF11-11BD-23CE-4689-2020-11-03

He fills in his selections using a number 2 pencil, slips his ballot through the machine, which reads his selections and displays them for his validation and approval. He confirms what he sees on the screen and two receipts are printed, both in colored ink with watermarks along with the ballot UID and a confirmation listing of all selections. One copy is for his records, and the other he slips into a locked box which will remain sealed unless there is a call for an audit.

The system logs the selections and the UID who chose them in a database and runs the tallies from this information. The votes are logged immediately in both a secure DB with no direct internet access as well as a public server where the encrypted UIDs and gathered votes are stored as a public record because there’s no means of connecting the IDs to the users without both the decryption tool that provides the internal encrypted registration ID and direct access to the government database. This means every ballot is public record, while the voters themselves are protected. Voters can also review whether the public tally is capturing their votes correctly by simply looking up their ID hex and verifying the results were what they selected.

Transparency for the state, but privacy for the individual.
